\section[il rapporto]{il rapporto — relationship; report}

\label{lesson:IT-C494-rapporto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for relatives, then the Italian for to look like.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il rapporto}
\textbf{il rapporto} — \textquotedblleft{}relationship; report\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho un buon rapporto con i miei genitori.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have a good relationship with my parents.}
\end{quote}

At work, \emph{un rapporto} can also be a report.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rapporto} is built on \emph{rapportare} \textquotedblleft{}to bring back, to report\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{ri-}, \emph{a-} and \emph{portare} \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{portāre} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il rapporto}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il rapporto}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il rapporto}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for relatives, then the Italian for to look like, then say \emph{il rapporto} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il rapporto mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Relationship; report\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[separarsi]{separarsi — to separate, to split up}

\label{lesson:IT-C494-separarsi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to look like, then the Italian for relationship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: separarsi}
\textbf{separarsi} — \textquotedblleft{}to separate, to split up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
I miei genitori si sono separati quando ero piccolo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My parents separated when I was little.}
\end{quote}

It takes \emph{essere}. \emph{Separati} — separated, not yet divorced.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{separarsi} is the reflexive of \emph{separare}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sēparāre} \textquotedblleft{}to part, to divide\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{sē-} \textquotedblleft{}apart\textquotedblright{} and \emph{parāre}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{separarsi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{separarsi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{separarsi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to look like, then the Italian for relationship, then say \emph{separarsi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does separarsi mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To separate, to split up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la separazione]{la separazione — separation}

\label{lesson:IT-C494-separazione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for relationship, then the Italian for to separate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la separazione}
\textbf{la separazione} — \textquotedblleft{}separation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dopo la separazione lui è andato a vivere da solo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the separation he went to live alone.}
\end{quote}

In law it comes before the divorce.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{separazione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sēparātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a severing\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{sēparāre}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la separazione}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la separazione}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la separazione}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for relationship, then the Italian for to separate, then say \emph{la separazione} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la separazione mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Separation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[lasciarsi]{lasciarsi — to break up}

\label{lesson:IT-C494-lasciarsi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to separate, then the Italian for separation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: lasciarsi}
\textbf{lasciarsi} — \textquotedblleft{}to break up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ci siamo lasciati dopo tre anni insieme.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We broke up after three years together.}
\end{quote}

The reflexive of \emph{lasciare} \textquotedblleft{}to leave\textquotedblright{}: \emph{mi ha lasciato} — he left me.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lasciarsi} is the reflexive of \emph{lasciare} \textquotedblleft{}to leave\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{laxāre} \textquotedblleft{}to loosen, to release\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lasciarsi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lasciarsi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{lasciarsi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to separate, then the Italian for separation, then say \emph{lasciarsi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does lasciarsi mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To break up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[risposarsi]{risposarsi — to remarry}

\label{lesson:IT-C494-risposarsi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for separation, then the Italian for to break up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: risposarsi}
\textbf{risposarsi} — \textquotedblleft{}to remarry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dopo il divorzio mia madre si è risposata.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the divorce my mother remarried.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ri-} \textquotedblleft{}again\textquotedblright{} plus \emph{sposarsi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{risposarsi} is built from \emph{ri-} \textquotedblleft{}again\textquotedblright{} and \emph{sposarsi} \textquotedblleft{}to marry\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{spōnsāre} \textquotedblleft{}to betroth\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{spondēre} \textquotedblleft{}to promise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{risposarsi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{risposarsi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{risposarsi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for separation, then the Italian for to break up, then say \emph{risposarsi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does risposarsi mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To remarry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Ripasso dei capitoli 487–494}

\label{lesson:IT-R494-ripasso-487-494}



\begin{quote}
Say the Italian for to chew and to digest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to chew, to digest, feeling unwell, to vomit, dizziness
  \item emergency room, to admit to hospital, surgeon, to operate, anaesthesia
  \item to fall ill, symptom, diagnosis, infection, to recover
  \item insomnia, to snore, nightmare, to yawn, to stretch
  \item crush, to court, sweetheart, tenderness, kiss
  \item hug, to cuddle, cuddles, to grow fond of, affectionate
  \item brother-in-law, sister-in-law, great-grandfather, relatives, to look like
  \item relationship, to separate, separation, to break up, to remarry
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To chew? (\textbf{masticare}.) To digest? (\textbf{digerire}.) Feeling unwell? (\textbf{il malessere}.) To vomit? (\textbf{vomitare}.) Dizziness? (\textbf{le vertigini}.) Emergency room? (\textbf{il pronto soccorso}.) To admit to hospital? (\textbf{ricoverare}.) Surgeon? (\textbf{il chirurgo}.) To operate? (\textbf{operare}.) Anaesthesia? (\textbf{l'anestesia}.) To fall ill? (\textbf{ammalarsi}.) Symptom? (\textbf{il sintomo}.) Diagnosis? (\textbf{la diagnosi}.) Infection? (\textbf{l'infezione}.) To recover? (\textbf{guarire}.) Insomnia? (\textbf{l'insonnia}.) To snore? (\textbf{russare}.) Nightmare? (\textbf{l'incubo}.) To yawn? (\textbf{sbadigliare}.) To stretch? (\textbf{sgranchirsi}.) Crush? (\textbf{la cotta}.) To court? (\textbf{corteggiare}.) Sweetheart? (\textbf{l'innamorato}.) Tenderness? (\textbf{la tenerezza}.) Kiss? (\textbf{il bacio}.) Hug? (\textbf{l'abbraccio}.) To cuddle? (\textbf{coccolare}.) Cuddles? (\textbf{le coccole}.) To grow fond of? (\textbf{affezionarsi}.) Affectionate? (\textbf{affettuoso}.) Brother-in-law? (\textbf{il cognato}.) Sister-in-law? (\textbf{la cognata}.) Great-grandfather? (\textbf{il bisnonno}.) Relatives? (\textbf{la parentela}.) To look like? (\textbf{assomigliare}.) Relationship? (\textbf{il rapporto}.) To separate? (\textbf{separarsi}.) Separation? (\textbf{la separazione}.) To break up? (\textbf{lasciarsi}.) To remarry? (\textbf{risposarsi}.)
